help.howitworks.switching_service_source.backTranslation: Why the choices change: a source that fails permanently, a service that is disabled, unavailable, out of quota or not included in your subscription, or a download that has completed, disappears from the lists or is shown as unavailable. Switching back and forth does not by itself remove a choice.

Progress: when choosing a source would discard progress already made, DebridPulse first asks Discard downloaded progress?. A service switch that would discard progress is instead refused, with the reason would discard downloaded data; switch the link's source to confirm.

While a download is paused: choosing another source for a file that had already started downloading is accepted and saved, but nothing starts. The service and source shown remain the current ones, and next to the service name a message names where the file is going, for example Switch to Real-Debrid (rapidgator.net) on resume. Choosing again replaces this; choosing the source already in use removes it. After you resume, it says Switching to … until the switch takes effect, after which it disappears. If a download's paused files would go to different places, or if the destination is not known, no destination is shown. A file that never started has nothing to transfer; the new source therefore simply applies when it starts. Choosing a service while the download is paused works as described above, except that the download stays paused: a service that can take over the link in use takes it over immediately (the badge shows that), and a service that must first prepare a copy shows … preparing… and only takes over after you resume. These messages appear in the rows of Download Activity and Downloads; both kinds can appear at the same time.

help.howitworks.backup_torrents.each_deb.backTranslation: Each debrid service has a Prepare backup torrents switch. It is on by default for AllDebrid, Debrid-Link, Premiumize and Real-Debrid, and off by default for TorBox, which has stricter torrent limits. While it is on, that service also adds torrents that another service is delivering, so that it is ready to take over if needed; and when you switch a download to another service, the torrent that had already been started is kept as a backup instead of removed. This uses that account's torrent slots and limits; a new download that needs a slot takes it back first. Turn the switch off to keep that service's slots for its own downloads: its backup torrents are then removed. A choice you have already saved is kept.

help.howitworks.adding_same_thing.if_add.backTranslation: If you add a magnet, {file_type} file, NZB or Metalink file that DebridPulse is already working on (including one that failed and was not removed), it shows Already in queue and keeps the existing download instead of starting a second one. Web links are always added as a new download. Once a download is completed, cancelled or removed, adding the same source again starts a new download. When two downloads turn out to fetch the same content, DebridPulse can consolidate them; the consolidated download shows Consolidated. When DebridPulse cannot prove that they match, the consolidated download instead shows Consolidated · Not verified. Consolidating changes nothing about who asked for it: each account's request stays that account's.

help.settings.users_access.user_accounts.backTranslation: User accounts shows every person with their role, their way of signing in and whether the account is enabled. Add local account creates an account with a username and password. A role changed in Edit user applies immediately: that person's open pages reload with the new role, without the person being signed out. Everyone has a DebridPulse username, separate from the display name: an OIDC account gets it at first sign-in, and it is the name with which someone signs in with a local password; the pencil next to it in the title of Edit user changes that name and keeps any stored password. Click an account's name for its details and activity; there a pending request can be revoked individually. Disable and Remove first show how many pending download requests the account has; those requests are revoked, a transfer that someone else also asked for continues, and completed downloads are never touched. Disabling also ends the account's sign-ins and stops its tokens; removing keeps the account's history and deletes its own notification settings. A removed OIDC sign-in that comes back gets a new account that stays disabled until you enable it. Merge merges two or more accounts into the account you want to keep; two accounts with the same verified email address are flagged, but only Merge merges them. DebridPulse always keeps at least one usable Admin, and you cannot change your own role or disable your own account.

help.topic.delivery_profiles.jobs_files..backTranslation: Submitting a job creates a download request that belongs to that application. If the job is removed in the application, that request is withdrawn, or the delivery is confirmed once it is complete; the transfer itself only stops if nobody else still needs it.
Completed files are shared in place: nothing is copied, linked or moved for the application, and confirming or expiring a delivery does not delete any file.

help.topic.deployment_type.what_switchin.backTranslation: No account is deleted. Other people's accounts keep their username, password, links with identity providers and stored Enabled or Disabled status. In Standalone they cannot sign in, regardless of what that status indicates.
It clears the built-in Admin's password, turns off signing in with Username and password and with OpenID Connect, and ends every browser session.
Afterwards no sign-in is needed: anyone who can reach DebridPulse at an address it accepts can use it as the built-in Admin. This is not limited to this computer and does not expire.
